context.alert_text: Throttles on the checkout API function above 10 per minute for 3 minutes

root_cause.hypothesis: The function's reserved concurrency is capped at 5 (C5, M3), and concurrent executions are pinned at that ceiling (M8) while invocations (1630) far exceed capacity, so Lambda throttles the excess - consistent with near-zero errors/log issues (M4, M9) indicating the function itself runs fine but can't get enough concurrency slots.
evidence: C2 PutFunctionConcurrency change just before alarm
M4 lambda_errors=0 rules out code-level failures
ruled_out: Code/runtime errors causing throttles (M4 errors=0, M9 log_error_lines=0)
Deploy of new version causing regression (D1 shows version 58 deployed but duration/memory metrics look normal per F3)

proposal.reasoning: Throttles (4812) correlate directly with concurrent executions being capped at the reserved concurrency limit of 5 (M3, M8), while invocation volume (1630) and healthy duration/memory metrics (F3) show the function itself is performing normally. Raising the reserved concurrency limit removes the artificial ceiling causing requests to be throttled.
proposal.expected_effect: Lambda will be able to scale concurrent executions beyond 5, reducing or eliminating throttles for warden-dev-checkout-api while leaving code and other config unchanged.
